{{Tooltip|L|Lost}} 60–75 vs. [[2023–24 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|Connecticut]] }} {{2023–24 Big Ten Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2023–24 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team''' represented [[Purdue University]] in the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Their head coach was [[Matt Painter]], who was in his 19th season with the Boilermakers. The Boilermakers played their home games at [[Mackey Arena]] in [[West Lafayette, Indiana]] as members of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. The Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team drew an average home attendance of 14,876 in 16 games in 2023–24.[http://fs.ncaa.org.s3.amazonaws.com/Docs/stats/m_basketball_RB/Attend.pdf MEN’S BASKETBALL ATTENDANCE RECORDS THROUGH 2023-24] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250109032519/http://fs.ncaa.org.s3.amazonaws.com/Docs/stats/m_basketball_RB/Attend.pdf |date=January 9, 2025 }} With their win over [[2023–24 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] on March 2, 2024, Purdue clinched a share of their 26th Big Ten regular season championship.{{cite web |url=https://bigten.org/news/2024/3/2/general-purdue-clinches-share-of-2023-24-big-ten-conference-mens-basketball-title.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240303052829/https://bigten.org/news/2024/3/2/general-purdue-clinches-share-of-2023-24-big-ten-conference-mens-basketball-title.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 3, 2024 |title=Purdue Clinches Share of 2023-24 Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Title |website=BigTen.org |date=March 2, 2024 |access-date=March 4, 2024}} Three days later, the Boilermakers clinched the Big Ten title outright for the second consecutive year with their victory over [[2023–24 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]].{{cite news |last=Stein |first=Steve |url=https://www.standard-journal.com/sports/local/article_809a8ee9-94b3-57bc-bfae-1d59a9c47674.html |title=Purdue clinches outright Big Ten title |date=March 6, 2024 |work=The Standard-Journal |access-date=March 6, 2024 |archive-date=March 7, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240307211135/https://www.standard-journal.com/sports/local/article_809a8ee9-94b3-57bc-bfae-1d59a9c47674.html |url-status=live }} The team finished the season 34–5, 17–3 in [[2023–24 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]]. They defeated Michigan State in the quarterfinals of the [[2024 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]] before losing to [[2023-24 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] in the semifinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 1 seed in the Midwest region. It marked the second consecutive year as a No. 1 seed.{{Cite web |last=Schofield |first=Mark |date=2024-03-17 |title=NCAA men's bracket 2024: The full ranking seed list, from No. 1 to No. 68 |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2024/3/17/24100820/ncaa-mens-bracket-2024-rankings |access-date=2024-03-18 |website=SBNation.com |language=en |archive-date=March 18, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240318001729/https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2024/3/17/24100820/ncaa-mens-bracket-2024-rankings |url-status=live }} They defeated [[2023–24 Grambling State Tigers men's basketball team|Grambling State]] and [[2023–24 Utah State Aggies men's basketball team|Utah State]] to break the school record of most wins in a season.{{Cite web |date=March 24, 2024 |title=The most wins in school history. |url=https://x.com/BoilerBall/status/1772006941658599858?s=20 |access-date=March 24, 2024 |archive-date=December 15, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241215101712/https://x.com/BoilerBall/status/1772006941658599858?s=20 |url-status=live }} They defeated [[2023–24 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]] in the Sweet Sixteen and defeated [[2023-24 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]] in the Elite Eight to return to the Final Four for the first time since [[1980 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|1980]]. In the Final Four, they defeated [[2023–24 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]] to advance to the National Championship game, their first since [[1969 NCAA University Division basketball championship game|1969]], where they lost to No. 1 overall seed [[2023–24 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]]. The season saw several new program records. In addition to most wins in a season, Purdue set school records in points (3,211), rebound margin (+11.2), assists (720), assist / turnover ratio (1.63), field goals made (1,109), free throws made (675), and free throws attempted (938).{{Cite web |title=Purdue celebrates record-breaking season ending in final four run |url=https://purduesports.com/news/2024/4/17/mens-basketball-purdue-celebrates-record-breaking-season-ending-in-final-four-run |access-date=May 8, 2024 |archive-date=May 8, 2024
